questions.question: Two taps J and L can fill a tank alone in 10 minutes and 12 minutes respectively. If an outlet tap K is opened and all three taps work together, then the same tank will be filled in 15 minutes. How much time will tap K alone take to empty the same tank?
questions.solution:
Given:

Two taps J and L can fill a tank alone in 10 minutes and 12 minutes respectively.

An outlet tap K is opened and all three taps work together, then the same tank will be filled in 15 minutes.

Concept used:

Efficiency = (Total work / Total time taken)

Efficiency = work done in a single day 

Calculation:

Let total work is 60 units ( LCM of 10,12 and 15) 

The efficiency of J is, 60 /10 = 6 

The efficiency of L is, 60 /12 = 5 

Combined efficiency is, 60 /15 = 4

The efficiency of K is, 6 + 5 - 4 = 7 unit

**So, K alone can empty it in 60 / 7 minutes**

questions.question: Suraj starts his journey from point Q at 2 p.m. He drives the car at the speed of 40 km/hr for first three hours and complete the remaining journey at the speed of 30 km/hr. If Rahul starts moving towards Suraj at 6 p.m. from point Q at the speed of 80 km/hr, then at what time he will catch Suraj?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Suraj starts his journey from point Q at 2 p.m.

He drives the car at the speed of 40 km/hr for first three hours and complete the remaining journey at the speed of 30 km/hr.

Rahul starts moving towards Suraj at 6 p.m.from point Q at the speed of 80 km/hr.

**Concept used**:

Distance = speed × time

**Calculation:**

The total distance is Covered till 6 pm by Suraj is (40 × 3 + 30} = 150km

The relative speed between Rahul and Suraj is 80 -30 = 50km

So the time taken by Rahul to meet him is 150 /50 = 3hr

They will meet at 6pm + 3 hr = 9: 00 pm

**∴ The correct option is 2**

questions.question: A group of boys has an average weight of 42 kg. One boy weighing 48 kg leaves the group and another boy weighing 38 kg joins the group. If the average now becomes 41 kg, then how many boys are there in the group?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net change in total weight = New boy's weight − Old boy's weight = 38 − 48 = −10 kg

Change in average weight = New average − Old average = 41 − 42 = −1 kg

Total number of boys = Net change in total weight ÷ Change in average

⇒ Total boys = −10 ÷ −1 = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10 boys.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial average weight of a group of boys = 42 kg

Weight of the boy who leaves = 48 kg

Weight of the boy who joins = 38 kg

New average weight of the group = 41 kg

 
 Initial Group: n boys × 42 kg
 
 

 

 Leaves: −48 kg
 
 

 

 Joins: +38 kg
 
 
 Final Group: n boys × 41 kg
 
 Net Change in Total Weight = 38 − 48 = −10 kg

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations

**Calculations:**

Let the number of boys in the group be n.

⇒ Total initial weight of the group = 42 × n = 42n

When one boy weighing 48 kg leaves and another boy weighing 38 kg joins:

⇒ New total weight = 42n − 48 + 38 = 42n − 10

The new average weight of the n boys becomes 41 kg.

⇒ New total weight = 41 × n = 41n

Equating the two expressions for the new total weight:

⇒ 42n − 10 = 41n

⇒ 42n − 41n = 10

⇒ n = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10 boys.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Net Change in Averages

When an item is replaced, Number of Items = (Value of new item − Value of old item) ÷ (New Average − Old Average).

Weighted Average

If group A has n₁ items with average A₁ and group B has n₂ items with average A₂, then combined average = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Impact of Addition/Subtraction

If a constant value 'k' is added to or subtracted from all observations, the new average also increases or decreases by 'k'.
</p

questions.question: What is the least number which when divided by 8, 10, 12 and 18 leaves a remainder 5 in each case?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The required number leaves a remainder of 5 when divided by 10.

This means the unit digit of the number must be 5.

Checking the given options, only 365 has a unit digit of 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 365.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors: 8, 10, 12 and 18

Remainder: 5 in each case

**Formula Used:**

Required Least Number = LCM(Divisors) + Remainder

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a4d9b0a57af2cd8b2887d2597011c4f0d51dc79a8e76d40858f298f52bd605ef.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 8 = 2³

⇒ Prime factorization of 10 = 2 × 5

⇒ Prime factorization of 12 = 2² × 3

⇒ Prime factorization of 18 = 2 × 3²

⇒ LCM = Highest power of each prime factor = 2³ × 3² × 5

⇒ LCM = 8 × 9 × 5 = 360

⇒ Required Number = 360 + 5 = 365

**∴ The correct answer is 365.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM (Least Common Multiple)

The smallest positive integer that is uniformly divisible by all given numbers.

HCF (Highest Common Factor)

The largest positive integer that divides each of the given numbers without leaving a remainder.

Same Remainder Case

If a number when divided by a, b, c leaves the same remainder r, then the Least Number = LCM(a, b, c) + r.

Different Remainders Case

If divided by a, b, c leaves remainders p, q, r such that (a−p) = (b−q) = (c−r) = k, then the Least Number = LCM(a, b, c) − k.

questions.question: 8 women can complete a work in 15 days. If 2 women are employed, then in how many days the work will be completed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

8 women can complete a work in 15 days.

**Concept used:**

Total work = Number of women employed × number of days required

**Calculation:**

Total work is 15 × 8 = 120 unit

If 2 women are employed, then number of days the work will be completed is 120 / 2 = 60 days

**∴ The correct option is 1**

questions.question: A man bought two flats for Rs. 6075000 each. He sold, one flat at 10% gain and other at 15% loss. How much percent he gain or lose in the whole?
questions.solution:

A man bought two flats for Rs. 6075000 each.

He sold, one flat at 10% gain and other at 15% loss.

**Concept used:**

The cost price is the same.

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price is 100 unit

Then gain is 100 × 10/100 = 10 unit

Loss is 100 × 15/100 = 15 unit

overall loss is 15 - 10 = 5 units

So loss percentage is (5 /200) × 100 = 2.5 %

**∴ The correct option is 1**

By putting the value of A,B and C we get

= 5 : 8 : 7

questions.question: The length of a cuboid is half of its breadth and the height of cuboid is thrice of its breadth. If the breadth of the cuboid is 12 cm, then what is the total surface area of cuboid?
questions.solution:
Given:

The length of a cuboid is half of its breadth and the height of the cuboid is thrice of its breadth.

The breadth of the cuboid is 12 cm.

Formula used:

The total surface area of a cuboid = 2 ×(lb× bh × lh)

(l = length, b = breadth , h = height)

Calculation: 

The height of the cuboid will be

⇒ 3 × 12 = 36 cm

The length of the cuboid will be

⇒ 12 /2 = 6 cm

the total surface area will be,

⇒ 2 ×(lb+ bh + lh)

⇒ 2 ×(36× 6 + 36 × 12 + 12 × 6)

⇒ 1440 cm2

∴ The correct option is 2
